title: Practical contextual bandits for large-scale structured discrete constrained optimization problems

problem.claim: Contextual bandit learning must handle high-dimensional combinatorial action spaces with structured discrete optimization constraints, while estimating objective- and constraint-related quantities from trial data.

gap.claim: The setting requires a practical approach that can integrate flexible predictors, represent large action spaces efficiently, and manage exploration, exploitation, and constraint-related reward non-smoothness.

contributions.claim: A contextual bandit approach based on general-purpose regression oracles and Inverse Gap Weighting integrated with an optimization framework.

An IGW sampling procedure using column generation to reformulate the underlying MIP model, supporting flexible lower-level predictors, causal coherence, and efficient large-action-space representation.
A risk-averse phased learning strategy for handling non-smooth rewards caused by optimization constraints.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe their approach as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The approach was validated on a real-world auto-scaling problem in IT automation.
The authors report a significant reduction in cumulative regret through exploration.
The authors report additional gains from risk-averse methods in managing constraint violations.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work addresses contextual bandits over high-dimensional combinatorial action spaces with structured discrete constraints.

Optimization quantities affecting objectives and constraints must be estimated from data during sequential action trials, with applications including IT resource allocation and retail assortment price optimization.
The authors propose a regression-oracle approach using IGW, column generation, a diverse solution pool, and risk-averse phased learning.
The authors report real-world auto-scaling validation with reduced cumulative regret and improved constraint-violation management.

source_observation.claim: Column generation and a diverse solution pool are used to make IGW sampling practical in large structured action spaces.

interpretation.claim: Separating large-action-space representation from exploration-pool construction may help preserve tractability while maintaining exploration.

application.claim: Consider optimization reformulations and solution-pool strategies when deploying contextual bandits over structured discrete decisions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this strategy transfers to settings without comparable MIP structure or solution-pool generation.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify baselines, dataset scale, experimental protocol, or quantitative regret values.
The abstract does not provide details of the regression oracles, phased-learning schedule, or constraint-violation metrics.
